content.title: Brazil stocks slip, real rebounds after Trump's 50% tariff threat
content.summary: LONDON/NEW YORK (Reuters) -Brazil's stock market was dragged lower by its financial sector on Thursday while the real currency rebounded, a day after U.S. President Donald Trump's shock move to slap 50% tariffs on imports from Latin America's largest economy, citing political disagreements.  U.S.-listed shares of Brazilian companies fell, with a widely followed Brazil ETF down 1.6%.  The main local stock market index shed 0.5%.
